$comment: Example entries. Not shown in the registries; used to preview entry.html (?src=example) and to test scripts/validate.py. Each card field explains what belongs in it.

models.title: Example model entry
models.summary: A placeholder that shows how a released model is laid out, with every field of the model card filled.
models.citation: Author One and Author Two (2026). Example model entry, version 1.0.0. XUrbanAI. https://xurbanai.com/entry.html?registry=models&id=example-model

card.urban_question: State the city problem in one or two sentences, and name the people who will use the output. A model without a stated user does not enter the registry.
card.intended_task: Name the task precisely, for example a rating, a classification, or an embedding, and the decision it is meant to inform.
card.inputs_modalities: List each input with its resolution and preprocessing, for example street-level images at 640 by 640 pixels, cropped and colour-normalised.
card.data_provenance: Give every training source with its geography, period, licence, and sampling. Say what was excluded and why.
card.evaluation:
Report held-out results against at least one baseline, with uncertainty. Link the evaluation code so the numbers can be reproduced.

Results are reported exactly as released; later re-runs get a new version.
card.failure_modes: Describe observed errors, gaps between subgroups or neighbourhoods, and the conditions under which outputs should not be used.
card.geographic_validity: Name the cities used for training and testing, and state whether any claim of transfer to other places is supported by evidence.
card.usage_constraints: Name the intended users, prohibited uses, and where human review is required before outputs inform a decision.

agents.title: Example agent entry
agents.summary: A placeholder that shows how a released agent is laid out, including its decision boundaries and audit trail.
agents.citation: Author One (2026). Example agent entry, version 0.3.0. XUrbanAI.

card.urban_question: State the planning or research task the agent supports, and who runs it.
card.task_workflow: Describe the steps in order, where the workflow starts, and where it hands back to a person.
card.data_provenance: List the models, datasets, APIs, and documents the agent can call or read, with their licences.
card.decision_boundaries: Say what the agent may decide alone and what always requires a human, and how outputs are reviewed.
card.evaluation: Define success, report reliability across repeated runs, and compare with people doing the same task.
card.failure_modes: Describe fabrication risks, bias in retrieved evidence, and misuse scenarios that were tested.
card.traceability: Describe the logs, intermediate outputs, and citations the agent produces so that a result can be audited.
card.geographic_validity: Name the places where the workflow was tested and whether results hold elsewhere.
card.usage_constraints: Name settings where the agent must not be used, and any cost or rate limits.

benchmarks.title: Example benchmark entry
benchmarks.summary: A placeholder that shows how a released benchmark is laid out, from task definition to submission rules.
benchmarks.citation: Author One, Author Two and Author Three (2026). Example benchmark entry, version 1.1.0. XUrbanAI.

card.urban_question: Name the capability the task measures and why it matters for an urban decision.
card.task_definition: Give the inputs, expected outputs, and the exact instructions or prompts a system under test receives.
card.data_provenance: Give the source, geography, period, licence, and splits, and explain how test data is kept from leaking into training.
card.metrics: Define the scoring rule, what counts as success, and how uncertainty or disagreement is reported.
card.baselines: List reference systems with their scores, including a simple baseline and a human baseline where one exists.
card.evaluation: Explain how the task itself was checked, for example annotation agreement and leakage tests.
card.failure_modes: Describe how the benchmark could be gamed or misread, and what it does not measure.
card.geographic_validity: Describe how performance is tested beyond the development data: other cities, periods, or populations.
card.submission_rules: Explain how results are submitted, what must be disclosed, and how the evaluation code is run.
card.versioning_errata: Record each version and correction. Version 1.1.0 corrected two mislabelled items in the test split; earlier results are reported against 1.0.0.
